QF.id: I Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_41

question.text: Fixed Deposit Receipts (FDRs) accepted as collateral from a trading member or clearing member should NOT be issued by:

answer.text: Banks that are associates of the trading member or clearing member
Any foreign bank operating in India

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook restriction on associate banks applies to Fixed Deposit Receipts (FDRs) issued in favour of the Clearing Corporation by trading or clearing members; such FDRs should not be issued by banks that are associates of the TM/CM, to avoid conflict of interest. "Associate" is defined under the SECC Regulations 2012. The Trap: The restriction is on the relationship between the issuing bank and the TM/CM, not on the bank's category (nationalised, private, or foreign). Bank guarantees from clients are governed by separate single-bank-exposure rules and should not be confused with this FDR restriction. Note: The associate-bank rule prevents a failing TM/CM from supporting its own collateral position with an FDR issued by a bank within its own group.
